findings.body: ActiveRecord's collection association expects a User record here and can raise a type-mismatch exception, so member removal fails with a server error.
findings.failure_mode: The removal action cannot complete successfully for normal administrator requests.
findings.impact: ActiveRecord's collection association expects a User record here and can raise a type-mismatch exception, so member removal fails with a server error.
findings.root_cause: The new endpoint forwards the raw integer request parameter to `group.users.delete` instead of providing a User instance or deleting the join record.
findings.suggested_fix: Load the user record before deleting it, or delete the matching GroupUser directly, for example `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).destroy_all`.
findings.title: Removing a member passes an integer to the association
findings.trigger: An administrator sends the new DELETE `/admin/groups/:group_id/members` request with a valid numeric `user_id`.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 90 shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id` is an integer. ActiveRecord's `has_many :users, through: :group_users` association's `delete` method expects a User record or array of records, not an integer ID. This will fail to remove the user correctly. The Group model at line 8 confirms `has_many :users, through: :group_users`.

findings.body: The UI reports an extra page, requests an empty offset, and displays an empty member list for that page.
findings.failure_mode: Navigation state and displayed membership diverge from the actual number of pages.
findings.impact: The UI reports an extra page, requests an empty offset, and displays an empty member list for that page.
findings.root_cause: The pagination formula treats every nonempty collection as if it had a remainder page.
findings.suggested_fix: Calculate the ceiling of `user_count / limit` rather than always adding one after flooring.
findings.title: Exact page-size groups expose a nonexistent extra page
findings.trigger: An administrator opens a group whose member count is an exact multiple of the page size, such as 50 members with a limit of 50, and clicks next.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 13 shows `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. For user_count=50 and limit=50, this yields floor(1)+1=2 pages when only 1 page exists. The correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. This creates a phantom extra page for exact multiples.

findings.body: The controller spec invokes the action directly with PUT even though the route is DELETE, so it does not verify that the configured DELETE endpoint reaches the protection logic.
findings.failure_mode: The test can pass while the real DELETE route is miswired or behaves differently.
findings.impact: The controller spec invokes the action directly with PUT even though the route is DELETE, so it does not verify that the configured DELETE endpoint reaches the protection logic.
findings.root_cause: The newly added test does not match the HTTP method introduced for `remove_member`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member` and add route/request coverage if necessary to verify the actual endpoint verb.
findings.title: The automatic-group removal test uses the wrong HTTP verb
findings.trigger: The test suite runs the new automatic-group removal example.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 115 shows `xhr :put, :remove_member` but the route at config/routes.rb:49 defines `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. The test uses PUT while the actual endpoint is DELETE. Line 125 correctly uses `:delete` for the success case, confirming the inconsistency.

raw_findings.title: Concurrent pagination requests can overwrite the current page with stale data
